judgment_text:
ORDER

The petitioner ist accused in C.C. No. 319 of 2022 on the file of the learned Special principal District and Sessions Judge, for EC and NDPS Act cases, Madurai. By judgment dated 30-12-2022, the petitioner was found guilty for the offence under Section 8(c) r/w 20(b)(ii)(C) and 29(i) of NDPS Act and convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs 1,00,000, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 6 months. Challenging the judgment of conviction and sentence, the petitioner has filed an appeal in Crl. A.(MD) No. 119 of 2023 and the same was admitted by this Court, by order dated 13-12-2023. Along with the appeal, the petitioner has also moved this petition seeking to suspend the sentence imposed by the trial court pending the appeal. This is the third application and the earlier applications were dismissed by this court.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the provisions under Section 57 and 52-A of the NDPS Act have not been complied with in this case. He further submits that all the witnesses are official witnesses and there is no independent witness. There is no corroboration among the evidence of the prosecution witnesses and no material has been produced to prove the case of the prosecution. There is delay of 5 days in sending the contraband to the court concerned. He is an innocent and he has been unnecessarily implicated in this case. He is in jail for more than 4 years. He is not having any bad antecedent.

3. The learned government advocate appearing for the respondent police submits that this is the 3rd petition and earlier petitions were dismissed by this court. He further submits there is no bad antecedent.

4. The petitioner has raised certain arguable points in this petition, which can be considered only during the final hearing of the appeal. However the appeal could not be taken up for final hearing for want of time. Considering the period of incarceration, for the reason that the appeal could not be taken up immediately despite the dismissal of the earlier applications and this Court is inclined to allow this petition.

5. Accordingly this petition is allowed and the substantive sentence of imprisonment imposed on the petitioner alone is suspended pending disposal of the criminal appeal on the following conditions:

(i) The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail on executing a bond for Rs 1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh) with two sureties each for a like sum to the satisfaction of the learned Special principal District and Sessions Judge, for EC and NDPS Act cases, Madurai.

(ii) The petitioner and the sureties shall file an affidavit before the respondent police that the petitioner will not misuse this liberty and will not indulge in any further offence. He will be available during this appeal proceedings.

(iii) The petitioner shall report before the respondent police daily at 10.30 am.

(iv) If the petitioner changes his residence, the same shall be informed to the respondent police immediately with correct address.

(v) If the petitioner violates any of the conditions, the respondent police shall move an application to cancel the order of suspension of sentence of imprisonment.
